The companies say they intend to explore deploying the vehicles in other right-hand-drive countries, including the UK. Waymo has been testing Jaguar I-Pace vehicles in London and says a robotaxi launch there would depend on receiving the necessary permits.

The partnership could also extend to autonomous technology in personally owned Toyota cars, but the companies have not set out what that would involve. Their earlier agreement was exploratory; the current announcement is more concrete on vehicle supply and testing than on a future service.

content.headline: TikTok launches restaurant guide built from videos and user reviews
content.shortHeadline: TikTok’s new restaurant guide draws on 40 million posts
content.standfirst: Must Eat lets users find local restaurants, browse related videos, leave reviews and make reservations. The feature is launching in a few US regions, putting TikTok in competition with review and mapping services.

sources.originalTitle: TikTok is going after Yelp and Google Maps with an in-app restaurant guide

segments.body: TikTok has launched Must Eat, an in-app restaurant guide built from 40 million posts, reviews and comments on the platform. Users can search a map, filter businesses, view related videos, leave reviews, call restaurants and make reservations.

segments.title: A new route from video to visit
segments.body: The guide separates listings into “everyday eats” and “elevated dining” and is initially available in New York City, Los Angeles and the Bay Area. TikTok says restaurants cannot pay to appear in recommendation lists. The company says 27 million US diners visited a restaurant, cafe or shop for the first time because of TikTok last year.

The launch builds on TikTok Go, which lets creators link to hotels and attractions. Must Eat also pushes the platform further into restaurant discovery, a space where creators’ food videos have already helped make some businesses popular and influenced how restaurants present dishes.

content.headline: Why video-game remakes keep bringing players back to familiar worlds
content.shortHeadline: Why game remakes trade on nostalgia—and risk disappointing fans
content.standfirst: Revisiting familiar games can revive shared memories and make older titles easier to play on modern hardware. But developers face a balancing act: update a classic without alienating fans or leaving players who want something new behind.

image.caption: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is often regarded as one of the greatest video games.

sources.originalTitle: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

segments.body: Game remakes offer more than updated graphics: they can let players revisit places tied to childhood memories and share those experiences with family or new generations. Players interviewed by the BBC described returning to games such as The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time and Final Fantasy VII as an emotional experience.

segments.title: A safe bet, with risks
segments.body: Reworking an established title can be less costly than developing a new game and gives companies an audience that already knows the original, says games analyst Piers Harding-Rolls. But fans can be protective of familiar games, and remakes may be criticised if changes feel wrong or if the result does not meet expectations.

Remakes can also make older games accessible on current devices, where original hardware may be difficult to use. Some developers expect future updates to focus less on graphics and more on reinterpretation or additional content; for others, nostalgia is no substitute for a genuinely new game.

content.headline: AI spending boom puts tech earnings and core businesses under pressure
content.shortHeadline: AI spending promises growth but tests tech giants’ core businesses
content.standfirst: Investors are weighing huge infrastructure bills against uneven returns: Google says AI search is affecting ad revenue, while Amazon plans to spend more even as cash flow turns negative. The companies argue the investments will pay off over time.

image.caption: The Google logo at the company’s headquarters in New York City.

sources.originalTitle: US tech stocks see sharp falls over AI cost fears
Google value plunges by $500bn as its own AI search hits ad sales
Amazon gives Wall Street mixed financial picture in earnings report
Google owner Alphabet loses $500bn in market value after profit disappoints Wall Street
US tech stocks see sharp falls over AI cost fears
Google value plunges by $500bn as its own AI search hits ad sales
AWS will be a $1T business, Jassy says — but first, it will spend big

segments.body: Tech shares fell as investors questioned the cost and returns of the AI build-out. Intel’s shares dropped sharply after it warned of a weaker PC market and rising investment; Amazon also came under pressure after reporting results that missed expectations. The Nasdaq opened at its lowest level in more than two months, according to the BBC.

segments.title: Google’s AI search trade-off
segments.body: Alphabet lost more than $500bn in market value after reporting lower-than-expected profit and slower growth in advertising. Google said its conversational AI search mode was eating into ad revenue alongside traditional results. Revenue rose 25% to $127.6bn, while Google Cloud revenue jumped 103% to $30.7bn.

perspectives.body: Former Google advertising executive Kim Scott described the decision to let AI summaries affect search ads as a long-term bet: Google would rather disrupt its own business than let a rival do it.

segments.body: Amazon’s Andy Jassy says the company expects about $220bn in capital spending in 2026, most of it for AWS, and plans to spend meaningfully more in 2027. Amazon reported negative $42bn in cash flow for the quarter in the BBC’s account; The Guardian reported AWS sales growth of 39.3%. Jassy argues the spending builds a business with substantial long-term potential, but investors remain concerned about the costs and timing of returns.

content.headline: OpenAI’s mathematics releases leave researchers struggling to verify results
content.shortHeadline: OpenAI’s math releases unsettle researchers as results pile up
content.standfirst: Sam Altman says OpenAI will keep publishing AI-generated mathematical findings, despite criticism that announcements lack context and verification. Researchers also object to the company withholding details of one claimed breakthrough.

sources.originalTitle: Sam Altman sympathizes with mathematicians, but says OpenAI’s math onslaught won’t stop

segments.body: OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman says the company will continue releasing mathematical results generated by its AI models, after researchers criticised a rapid stream of announcements they say is difficult to follow and verify. Altman acknowledged that the activity “got out of control” briefly, but said he believes the public deserves fundamental scientific knowledge.

segments.title: Release versus review
segments.body: Mathematicians told The Verge that some releases lacked adequate context, attribution and verification, leaving researchers to check and interpret the claims. The company has also faced criticism for withholding details of a claimed result involving Yang-Mills theory, saying it followed advice from a hand-picked group of experts.

Altman said OpenAI has spent hundreds of millions of dollars on mathematical problems, including about $10m on its proposed Navier-Stokes solution, and indicated it has more results not yet made public. The reporting describes the scale of the investment but does not establish that the results have been independently verified.

content.headline: AI data centres become a flashpoint in Maine’s expensive Senate race
content.shortHeadline: Maine Senate race turns on AI data-centre concerns and campaign cash
content.standfirst: Rural voters are raising concerns about power, water and promised jobs as data-centre development enters a high-spending Senate contest. The outcome could influence policy, while the candidates’ stances and local views are not simply divided along party lines.

sources.originalTitle: Maine’s data center revolt will decide who controls the Senate

segments.body: The expansion of data centres has become a contested issue in Maine’s Senate race, where rural voters have voiced concerns about water, electricity costs and whether projects will deliver lasting jobs. Towns have imposed temporary pauses or put development questions to voters; a September poll cited by The Verge found 76% opposed a data centre in their community.

segments.title: Promises and local doubts
segments.body: Developers and political allies promote jobs and tax revenue, but economic research cited in the report indicates that most data centres create little net employment after construction. Residents in former mill towns are weighing the prospect of investment against a history of boom-and-bust development and limited trust in companies’ promises.

The race has drawn major spending from technology and data-centre interests, especially on behalf of Republican senator Susan Collins. Her Democratic challenger, Troy Jackson, also supports development with guardrails, including union jobs. The report says the contest may help shape federal data-centre and AI policy, but does not establish how voters will ultimately respond to the spending.

content.headline: AI data-centre growth could reverse years of US power-sector emissions cuts
content.shortHeadline: Analysis warns AI data-centre demand could drive US emissions higher
content.standfirst: A Sierra Club analysis projects power-sector carbon dioxide emissions could be 42% higher in 2030 than in 2025 if planned AI projects are built and powered by fossil fuels. The estimate is higher than another study’s forecast and depends on what gets constructed.

sources.originalTitle: Data centers could send US climate pollution skyrocketing

segments.body: A Sierra Club analysis estimates that US power-sector carbon dioxide emissions could rise 42% by 2030 compared with 2025 if planned data-centre projects are built and fossil-fuel capacity expands to meet their electricity demand. The group says that would erase roughly 15 years of emissions reductions.

segments.title: A projection, not an outcome
segments.body: The Sierra Club estimates that electricity generation would produce an additional 618 million tons of carbon dioxide by the end of the decade under that scenario. Its projection is higher than an academic study published in June, which forecast a 28% increase in power-sector emissions by 2030 compared with a scenario without data-centre growth.

The outcome depends on how many proposed data centres are built and what powers them. The analysis comes from the Sierra Club, and the reporting notes that the US is planning more fossil-fuel capacity than it has in a decade; it does not establish that all planned projects will proceed.

content.headline: More than half of surveyed Victorian lawyers now use AI, study finds
content.shortHeadline: AI use rises among Victorian lawyers, but clients bring errors too
content.standfirst: A survey of 2,221 lawyers found 55% used AI in their work, up from 37% a year earlier. Many report correcting misleading AI-generated material brought in by clients, while only 26% said AI had lowered their fees.

image.caption: Illustrative image accompanying reporting on lawyers using AI and correcting client errors.

sources.originalTitle: More than half of Victorian lawyers use AI – but only a quarter have cut client fees as a result

segments.body: A census of 2,221 lawyers in the Australian state of Victoria found that 55% used AI in their practice in 2026, up from 37% the previous year. Use was highest in trade practices and banking and finance, and 79% of lawyers using AI said they used consumer chatbots such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or Copilot.

segments.title: Efficiency and fees
segments.body: Only 26% of respondents said AI use had reduced client fees. Researchers said verification may limit time savings; in the previous survey, 89% of practitioners said they checked AI output for accuracy. Some lawyers said AI let them take on work that had previously been uneconomical.

The survey also found 46% of lawyers said clients arrived with inaccurate or misleading information from AI, while 41% had received AI-generated documents requiring correction. Nearly half said clients’ AI use increased the time and effort needed to handle a matter.

content.headline: Wikimedia urges middle ground in AI copyright case over training and output
content.shortHeadline: Wikipedia’s operator draws a line between AI training and copied text
content.standfirst: The Wikimedia Foundation argues that training language models on copyrighted material can qualify as fair use, but reproducing that material for users may require a licence. It says an overly broad ruling could harm both open knowledge and useful AI tools.

sources.originalTitle: Wikipedia’s operator says a bad AI copyright ruling could threaten the open web

segments.body: The Wikimedia Foundation has urged a US court to avoid an all-or-nothing ruling in copyright lawsuits involving OpenAI and Microsoft. In a legal brief, the organisation says training AI on copyrighted works may be fair use when it produces something new, while chatbots that reproduce material in place of the original may need a licence.

segments.title: A two-way dependence
segments.body: Wikipedia is a major source of training data, but the foundation says AI services can draw visitors away from the sites and communities that maintain that knowledge. It also says AI tools could help editors detect vandalism, copyright violations and articles in need of improvement.

The foundation argues that output reproducing material should respect licensing terms, including attribution and Creative Commons requirements for Wikipedia content. It warns that a ruling too favourable to publishers could restrict transformative uses, while a sweeping victory for AI firms could weaken incentives for authors and fragment access to knowledge.

content.headline: DoorDash has received only hundreds of orders from third-party AI agents
content.shortHeadline: DoorDash reports just hundreds of orders via AI agents so far
content.standfirst: The delivery company says orders from outside AI agents remain tiny beside its roughly three million daily deliveries. Its chief executive says the field is evolving, and DoorDash is open to working with agent makers while developing its own tools.

sources.originalTitle: DoorDash said it’s only received ‘several hundred’ orders from AI agents

segments.body: DoorDash says it has received “several hundred” orders from third-party AI agents such as Muse and Instinct. That is a small number beside the roughly three million deliveries the company said it completed daily on average in 2025.

Chief executive Tony Xu said consumers still mainly order through DoorDash’s own app. He described agent-based ordering as a dynamic area and said the company wants to learn how it develops rather than assume it will quickly replace existing ways of ordering.

DoorDash has launched its own text-ordering and chatbot tools and an interface that allows ordering from other chatbots for corporate customers. Companies are still deciding whether to let third-party agents access their services; Amazon has blocked some agents, while Walmart has welcomed them.

content.headline: A humanist wins workplace exemption from using AI, raising wider questions
content.shortHeadline: University employee secures exemption from workplace AI use
content.standfirst: A University of Kentucky administrator says using AI conflicts with his humanist beliefs about exercising the mind. The university granted an accommodation for his role, while noting that requests are reviewed individually as job duties and technology change.

sources.originalTitle: You don’t need to believe in a god to get a religious exemption from using AI at work

segments.body: David Durman, a University of Kentucky administrator, has secured an accommodation allowing him to abstain from using AI at work. A nontheistic humanist, he says relying on AI could diminish people’s ability to act morally by applying their own minds.

segments.title: An individual accommodation
segments.body: Durman sought advice from the American Humanist Association, which says concerns about AI and human dignity can arise across faiths and traditions. The university said it reviews accommodation requests case by case, considering an employee’s duties and circumstances; it determined Durman could continue performing the essential functions of his position.

Durman says he pursued an accommodation before AI use becomes a workplace requirement. The university said arrangements may be reviewed as technology and job responsibilities evolve, so the case does not establish a general right for employees to refuse AI tools.

content.headline: Grealish left out as Everton beat Newcastle to reach EFL Cup quarters
content.shortHeadline: Everton drop Grealish and advance in the EFL Cup
content.standfirst: Everton beat Newcastle 3-1 without Jack Grealish, who was left out after what manager David Moyes called a breach of club discipline. The club has not disclosed further details.

image.caption: Jack Grealish, who has featured six times for Everton this season.

sources.originalTitle: Grealish dropped over 'breach of club discipline' - what now?

segments.body: Everton reached the EFL Cup quarter-finals with a 3-1 win over Newcastle, but Jack Grealish was absent after a breach of club discipline. David Moyes said the decision was the club’s and that he supported it; Everton gave no further details.

segments.title: What is known about the breach
segments.body: The absence is understood to have followed an unauthorised absence from training. Grealish returned to training and is expected to be fined, according to the report. Moyes would not say whether the on-loan Manchester City winger would return for Monday’s league game at Newcastle.

content.headline: Late PSG equaliser denies Manchester City a Women's Champions League win
content.shortHeadline: PSG hit back late to draw with Manchester City
content.standfirst: Khadija Shaw put City ahead with a late penalty, but Tara Elimbi Gilbert equalised three minutes later to earn Paris St-Germain a point. It was City's third draw in the competition.

sources.originalTitle: Women's Football

segments.body: Manchester City’s hopes of a Women's Champions League win were checked by a late Paris St-Germain equaliser. Khadija Shaw scored a penalty, but Tara Elimbi Gilbert levelled three minutes later; the draw was City’s third in the competition.

content.headline: South Africa's careless dismissals hand Australia the edge in Test decider
content.shortHeadline: Australia seize the edge after South Africa's poor strokes
content.standfirst: Australia lead by 40 with South Africa 140-4 at the close of day three in Cape Town. The hosts had been 100 behind after Australia made 429, and the series winner will finish top of the Test rankings.

sources.originalTitle: Careless dismissals give Australia route to series win

segments.body: South Africa reached 140-4 in their second innings at stumps, a lead of 40, after Australia made 429 in reply to the Proteas’ 329. The decisive third Test remains open, but Australia have the advantage after taking four wickets on day three.

segments.title: Wickets given away
segments.body: Aiden Markram drove Mitchell Starc to mid-off for one, while David Bedingham fell to a pull shot for the second time in the match. Temba Bavuma, who had helped rebuild the innings, was caught trying to force a shot late in the day. Australia still have work to do: South Africa have more batters to come, and Simon Harmer took four wickets in Australia's first innings.

content.headline: Alexander Zverev set to become men's world number one on Monday
content.shortHeadline: Zverev's Vienna win puts him on top of the rankings
content.standfirst: A straight-sets win over Tallon Griekspoor in Vienna means Zverev will replace Jannik Sinner at the top of the ATP rankings on Monday. He had already secured the year-end number one spot.

image.caption: Alexander Zverev, the 30th man to become ATP world number one.

sources.originalTitle: Zverev seals world number one spot after win

segments.body: Alexander Zverev beat Tallon Griekspoor 6-4 7-5 to reach the Vienna quarter-finals and secure the rise to world number one on Monday. The 29-year-old, who has won two Grand Slam titles this year, will be the second German to reach the top after Boris Becker.

segments.title: A standout season, with a caveat
segments.body: Zverev has won 64 of his 80 matches in 2026. Both of his major titles came with at least one of rivals Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz absent, and Zverev said he might not be the world's best if both were healthy and at their peak. He has nevertheless made the most of his opportunities this season.

content.headline: Duckett's 167 and Dawson's four wickets give England ODI consolation win
content.shortHeadline: Duckett and Dawson lead England to consolation win
content.standfirst: Ben Duckett made 167 and Liam Dawson took four wickets as England beat Sri Lanka by 55 runs in Lahore. England had already been eliminated from the tri-series final.

image.caption: Ben Duckett, who became the third England opener to pass 150 twice in ODIs.

sources.originalTitle: Duckett and Dawson deliver in England's consolation win

segments.body: England closed their ODI tri-series with a 55-run win over Sri Lanka. Ben Duckett made 167 from 132 balls as England posted 386-5; Sri Lanka were all out for 331, with Liam Dawson taking 4-49.

segments.title: An opening partnership to watch
segments.body: Duckett and Tom Banton added 163 for the first wicket, and Duckett made his second consecutive century. Banton has scored five half-centuries in his past six innings, giving England selectors a decision to make when Jacob Bethell returns from injury. Coach Brendon McCullum said the team would assess its options in Australia.

content.headline: Sergio Garcia quits LIV Golf and targets a Ryder Cup return
content.shortHeadline: Garcia leaves LIV and hopes to return to Europe's Ryder Cup team
content.standfirst: Garcia says he will rejoin the DP World Tour in 2027 and wants to make Europe's Ryder Cup team at Adare Manor. His departure comes as LIV tries to secure players and funding for its proposed next phase.

image.caption: Sergio Garcia won two individual titles in five seasons with LIV Golf.

sources.originalTitle: Garcia targets Ryder Cup return as he confirms LIV exit

segments.body: Sergio Garcia is leaving LIV Golf and plans to play on the DP World Tour in 2027. The 46-year-old, who won the 2017 Masters, said he is also keeping open the possibility of a return to the PGA Tour.

segments.title: A possible Ryder Cup return
segments.body: Garcia hopes to rejoin Europe's Ryder Cup team at Adare Manor next year, as a player or vice-captain. He was ineligible for the 2023 event after joining LIV and was not selected for the 2025 team, despite settling outstanding fines. Under current DP World Tour rules, he cannot serve as a future captain or vice-captain.

content.headline: England need a 68-point swing and Tonga win to reach Rugby League semi-finals
content.shortHeadline: England need big win and Tonga's help to stay alive
content.standfirst: England must beat Papua New Guinea convincingly and rely on Tonga beating Samoa to keep their semi-final hopes alive. Coach Brian McDermott has urged his side to stick to its plan rather than chase points too early.

sources.originalTitle: England boss McDermott urges patience in PNG points chase

segments.body: England need a 68-point swing in points difference against Samoa and a Tonga win over Samoa to avoid missing the Rugby League World Cup semi-finals for the first time. They face Papua New Guinea after beating France 82-0, but McDermott says they must be patient if the points do not come straight away.

segments.title: Selection for the challenge
segments.body: England have kept Matty Ashton on the left wing and selected Jez Litten at hooker, with Brad O'Neill among the interchanges. Morgan Knowles is set to play for the first time in the tournament after recovering from a calf problem. McDermott said the team was chosen for a tougher test than France.

content.headline: Elena Rybakina secures year-end women's world number one ranking
content.shortHeadline: Rybakina seals year-end number one after Tokyo win
content.standfirst: Rybakina beat Yulia Putintseva in Tokyo to make the year-end top spot unassailable. The Australian and US Open champion has won four titles in 2026 and took over as world number one in September.

image.caption: Elena Rybakina, whose first Grand Slam title came at Wimbledon in 2022.

sources.originalTitle: Rybakina secures year-end number one ranking

segments.body: Elena Rybakina secured the year-end women's singles number one ranking by beating Yulia Putintseva 6-2 6-3 in the Tokyo last 16. The result means she cannot be caught in the closing weeks of the season. She has won the Australian Open and US Open this year.

segments.title: A season built on momentum
segments.body: Rybakina also won the Ningbo Open last week, her fourth title of 2026. She first reached number one in September after a quarter-final win at the US Open, and said the year-end ranking was an achievement she had worked towards with her team.
